newsitem.title: USA: Seiler says German project to move ahead.
newsitem.headline: Seiler says German project to move ahead.

text.p: Seiler Pollution Control Systems Inc said Thursday it won approval from the German government to move ahead with a $12.7 million installation of a Seiler industrial high temperature vitrification system.
That translates to 18.6 marks, Seiler said in a statement.

Seiler systems convert hazardous wastes into glass ceramics usable by industry. In a demonstration project in Switzerland last spring, Seiler said it processed sludges from paint, industrial wastewater treatment and electroplating plus contaminated chemicals, petrochemicals, spent solvents, pesticides, asbestos-containing residuals and other wastes.
Construction of the Freiberg, Germany, facility is expected to begin immediately, Alan Sarko, Seiler vice president of North American operations, said in the statement.
Seiler said the German government secured a combination of grants and subsidies from the Dresdner Bank AG of Germany.

Under those arrangements, the bank will provide Seiler a long-term credit line of $6.8 million (9.9 million DM), with additional credit of $1.4 million (2.1 milllion DM) available if needed, Seiler said. In addition, Seiler said it expects $4.5 million (6.6 million DM) in German government grants.
